facts.statement: A Polish-Mongolian expedition discovered the fossil remains of Barsboldia in 1970 near the Nemegt locality.
facts.quote: In 1970, a Polish-Mongolian expedition near the Nemegt found the skeleton of an ornithopod and first assigned it to Saurolophus angustirostris.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold, and the species name honors technician Wojciech Siciński.
facts.quote: The genus name honors the Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold, while the species name honors Wojciech Siciński, the technician at the Warsaw Paleobiological Institute who prepared the skeleton.

facts.statement: Barsboldia was previously estimated to be 10 meters long and weigh 5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Barsboldia was a large hadrosaur, previously estimated at 10 m in length and 5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: A 2011 measurement of a 1.4-meter tibia suggests Barsboldia may have reached a total body length of 12 to 14 meters.
facts.quote: In 2011, the tibial length was measured at 1.4 m, rivaling that of Shantungosaurus at 1.47 m and that of Magnapaulia at 1.36 m; this indicates that Barsboldia could have possibly reached within the range of 12 - 14 m in total body length.

facts.statement: Barsboldia is distinguished by very tall neural spines, particularly over the hips, with club-shaped tips on the first few tail vertebrae that may indicate old age.
facts.quote: Similar to Ouranosaurus, the most distinctive features of Barsboldia are found in the neural spines. These are very tall, particularly over the hips, and were described as second only to those of Hypacrosaurus altispinus and the tips of those found in the first few vertebrae of the tail are club-shaped, possibly a sign of old age.

facts.statement: Maryańska and Osmólska originally classified Barsboldia as a lambeosaurine, the first such dinosaur described from the Nemegt Formation, despite the absence of a skull.
facts.quote: Maryańska and Osmólska described their new genus as a lambeosaurine (or hollow-crested duckbill), the first from the Nemegt Formation, although it lacked a skull.

facts.statement: Due to the lack of a skull and only one partial skeleton, the validity and placement of Barsboldia have been debated, with some considering it a dubious genus.
facts.quote: With only one partial skeleton known, and no skull, the genus has been considered dubious or a possible lambeosaurine of uncertain placement.

facts.statement: A 2011 study suggests that Barsboldia is a valid saurolophine rather than a lambeosaurine.
facts.quote: A newer study published in 2011 suggests that Barsboldia is actually a valid saurolophine.

facts.statement: As a hadrosaurid, Barsboldia was a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore with hundreds of continually-replaced teeth adapted for a grinding motion.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Barsboldia would have been a large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating plants with a sophisticated skull that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing, and was furnished with hundreds of continually-replaced teeth.

facts.statement: If Barsboldia was a lambeosaurine, it would have possessed a hollow crest used for visual and auditory identification.
facts.quote: If it was a lambeosaurine, it would have had a hollow crest formed out of expanded skull bones containing the nasal passages, with a function relating to identification by sight and sound.

facts.statement: The holotype sacrum of Barsboldia measured 10 meters in length, 4 meters in height, and weighed 2 tons.
facts.quote: Hueso sacro del holotipo Barsboldia medía 10 metros de longitud, 4 metros de altura y pesaba 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: The most distinctive features of the Barsboldia skeleton are the very tall neural spines, particularly over the hips, which are similar to those of Hypacrosaurus altispinus.
facts.quote: Las características más distintivas de este esqueleto se encuentran en las espinas neurales. Estas son muy altas, particularmente sobre las caderas, y fueron descritos como similares a los de Hypacrosaurus altispinus

facts.statement: Barsboldia fossils were discovered in Mongolia, representing one of the first hadrosaurid specimens found in Asia.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron descubiertos en Mongolia, uno de los primeros especímenes de hadrosáurido hallados en Asia.

facts.statement: Maryańska and Osmólska described Barsboldia as the first lambeosaurine, or hollow-crested duckbill, from the Nemegt Formation, although it lacked a skull.
facts.quote: Maryańska y Osmólska describen a este género como el primer Lambeosaurinae, o dinosaurio de pico de pato con cresta hueca, de la Formación Nemegt, aunque le faltara el cráneo.

facts.statement: A 2011 study suggests that Barsboldia is indeed a valid genus of saurolophine.
facts.quote: Un estudio publicado en 2011 sugiere que Barsboldia es de hecho un género válido de saurolofino.

facts.statement: Barsboldia lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Barsboldia is classified within the parent group Saurolophinae.
